content: Acute bronchitis is one of the most frequently diagnosed conditions in primary care settings. It is commonly treated with antibiotics, despite the fact that evidence supporting their effectiveness is weak and, at best, modest. Other treatments, which are even less effective, are also used. Chinese medicinal herbs have been proposed as an alternative treatment option for acute bronchitis. The objective of this review was to evaluate the existing evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness and safety of Chinese medicinal herbs in the treatment of uncomplicated acute bronchitis. To gather relevant data, a comprehensive search was conducted in multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, EMBASE, CNKI, and the Chinese Biomedical Database (CBM). The search covered studies published up to September 19, 2011. The review focused on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared Chinese medicinal herbs with placebo, antibiotics, or other Western medicines for the treatment of uncomplicated acute bronchitis. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed independently by at least two reviewers. However, none of the 74 studies involving 6877 participants that were identified as RCTs by the study authors met the inclusion criteria for this review. Among these studies, 39 were determined to be non-RCTs, and 35 involved comparisons between different Chinese herbal medicines in the intervention and control groups. The authors concluded that there is insufficient high-quality evidence to support the routine use of Chinese medicinal herbs for the treatment of acute bronchitis. The limitations in the design of the individual trials prevented any definitive conclusions regarding the potential benefits of these herbs. Furthermore, the safety profile of Chinese medicinal herbs remains unclear due to the lack of toxicological data, although some adverse events have been reported in case studies.
